entries.content: 35. wise — discreet or prudent. causeth shame — (Pr 10:5; 12:4) acts basely.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 15 Pr 15:1-33. 1. soft — tender or gentle. turneth... wrath — from any one. stir up — as a smouldering fire is excited.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. useth... aright — commends knowledge by its proper use. poureth out — utters abundantly (Pr 12:23), and so disgusts others.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. beholding — watching (compare Pr 5:21; Psa 66:7).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4. A wholesome tongue — (Compare Margin), pacifying and soothing language. tree of life — (Pr 3:18; 11:30). perverseness therein — cross, ill-natured language. breach... spirit — (compare Is 65:14, Hebrew), grieves, instead of appeasing.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5. (Compare Pr 4:1; 10:17; 13:1-18). is prudent — acts discreetly.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:6
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6. treasure — implying utility. trouble — vexation and affliction.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 7. (Compare Pr 10:20, 21). heart... not so — not right, or vain.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:8–9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8-9. The sacrifice [and] prayer — are acts of worship. way... followeth... righteousness — denote conduct. God's regard for the worship and deeds of the righteous and wicked respectively, so stated in Psa 50:17; Is 1:11.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. (Compare Pr 10:17). the way — that in which God would have him to go (Pr 2:13; Psa 119:1).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. Hell — (Psa 16:10). destruction — or, "Abaddon," the place of the destroyer. All the unseen world is open to God, much more men's hearts.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. (Compare Pr 9:8). go unto the wise — to be instructed.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. maketh... countenance — or, "benefits the countenance." spirit is broken — and so the countenance is sad.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. (Compare Pr 10:21, 22). The wise grow wiser, the fools more foolish (Pr 9:9).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. The state of the heart governs the outward condition. evil — sad, contrasted with the cheerfulness of a feast.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16. trouble — agitation, implying the anxieties and perplexities attending wealth held by worldlings (Pr 16:18; 1Ti 6:6).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. dinner — or, "allowance" (2Ki 25:30) — of herbs — and that the plainest. and hatred — (compare Pr 10:12, 18).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 15:19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19. The difficulties of the slothful result from want of energy; the righteous find a plain [and open] way — literally, "a highway," by diligence (1Sa 10:7; Psa 1:3).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. (Compare Pr 10:1).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21. walketh uprightly — and so finds his joy (Pr 3:6; 10:23).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22. Without counsel — or, "deliberation," implying a wise deference to the opinions of the wise and good, contrasted with rashness.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23. Good advice blesses the giver and receiver.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 24. (Compare Col 3:2). Holy purposes prevent sinning, and so its evils.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 25. The most desolate who have God's aid have more permanent good than the self-reliant sinner (Pr 2:22; 12:7). border — or, "boundary for possessions" (Psa 78:54).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:26
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26. are pleasant words — that is, pleasing to God (Pr 8:8, 9).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:27
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 27. (Compare Pr 11:17). Avarice brings trouble to him and his. hateth gifts — or, "bribes" (Ex 23:8; Psa 15:5), and is not avaricious.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:28
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 28. (Compare Pr 15:14; 10:11). Caution is the fruit of wisdom; rashness of folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:29
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 29. far... wicked — in His love and favor (Psa 22:11; 119:155).

entries.title: Proverbs 15:30
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 30. light of the eyes — (Pr 13:9). What gives light rejoiceth the heart, by relieving from anxiety as to our course; so good report — or, "doctrine" (Is 28:9; 53:1), maketh... fat — or, "gives prosperity" (Pr 3:13-17; 9:11). The last clause is illustrated by the first.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:31–32
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 31-32. (Compare Pr 10:17). reproof of life — which leads to life. abideth... wise — is numbered among them.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:33
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 33. The fear... wisdom — Wisdom instructs in true piety. before... humility — (compare Lu 24:26; 1Pe 1:11); opposite (compare Pr 16:18).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 16 Pr 16:1-33. 1. preparations — schemes. in man — or literally, "to man," belonging, or pertaining to him. the answer... Lord — The efficient ordering is from God: "Man proposes; God disposes."

entries.title: Proverbs 16:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. clean — or, "faultless." weigheth — or, "tries," "judges," implying that they are faulty (Pr 21:2; 24:12).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. (Compare Margin). Rely on God for success to your lawful purposes.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4. for himself — "for its answer," or "purpose," that is, according to God's plan; the wicked are for the day of evil (Psa 49:5; Jr 17:18); sinning and suffering answer to each other, are indissolubly united.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5. (Compare Pr 3:32).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:6
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6. By mercy and truth — that is, God's (Psa 85:10); He effects the atonement, or covering of sin; and the principles of true piety incline men to depart from evil; or, "mercy" and "truth" may be man's, indicative of the gracious tempers which work instrumentally in procuring pardon. purged — expiated (as in Le 16:33; Is 27:9, Hebrew).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 7. Persecutions, of course, excepted.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 16:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. (Compare Pr 16:3). directeth — establisheth.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. The last clause depends on the first, expressing the importance of equity in decisions, so authoritative.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. are the Lord's... his work — that is, what He has ordered, and hence should be observed by men.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. Rulers are rightly expected, by their position, to hate evil; for their power is sustained by righteousness.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. A specification of the general sentiment of Pr 16:12.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. This wrath, so terrible and certain, like messengers of death (1Ki 2:25), can be appeased by the wise.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. light of... countenance — favor (Psa 4:6). life — preserves it, or gives blessings which make it valuable. the latter rain — fell just before harvest and matured the crop; hence specially valuable (De 11:14).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 16:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. The highway — A common, plain road represents the habitual course of the righteous in departing from evil. keepeth — observes.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:18–19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18-19. (Compare Pr 15:33). Haughtiness and pride imply self-confidence which produces carelessness, and hence a fall — literally, "sliding."

entries.title: Proverbs 16:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. handleth a matter — wisely considers "the word," that is, of God (compare Pr 13:13). trusteth — (Compare Psa 2:12; 118:8, 9).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21. wise in heart — who rightly consider duty. sweetness of the lips — eloquent discourse, persuades and instructs others.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22. Understanding — or, "discretion," is a constant source of blessing (Pr 13:14), benefiting others; but fools' best efforts are folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23. The heart is the source of wisdom flowing from the mouth.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 24. (Compare Pr 15:26). Gentle, kind words, by soothing the mind, give the body health.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 25. (Compare Pr 14:2).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:26
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26. Diligence is a duty due to one's self, for his wants require labor.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:27
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 27. ungodly man — (Compare Pr 6:12). diggeth up evil — labors for it. in his lips... fire — His words are calumniating (Jas 3:6).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:28
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 28. (Compare Pr 6:14; 10:31). whisperer — prater, talebearer (Pr 18:8; 26:20).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:29
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 29. violent man — or, "man of mischief" (Pr 3:31). enticeth — (Pr 1:10).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:30
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 30. He shutteth his eyes — denoting deep thought (Psa 64:6). moving his lips — or, "biting his lips" — a determined purpose (Pr 6:13).

entries.title: Proverbs 16:31
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 31. (Compare Pr 20:29). if — or, which may be supplied properly, or without it the sense is as in Pr 3:16; 4:10, that piety is blessed with long life.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:32
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 32. (Compare Pr 14:29). taketh a city — that is, by fighting.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:33
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 33. Seemingly the most fortuitous events are ordered by God.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 17 Pr 17:1-28. 1. sacrifices — or, "feasts" made with part of them (compare Pr 7:14; Le 2:3; 7:31). with — literally, "of." strife — its product, or attendant.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. (Compare Pr 14:35). causeth shame — (Pr 10:5). shall... inheritance — that is, share a brother's part (compare Nu 27:4, 7).

entries.title: Proverbs 17:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. God only knows, as He tries (Psa 12:6; 66:10) the heart.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4. Wicked doers and speakers alike delight in calumny.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5. (Compare Pr 14:31). glad at calamities — rejoicing in others' evil. Such are rightly punished by God, who knows their hearts.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:6
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6. Prolonged posterity is a blessing, its cutting off a curse (Pr 13:22; Psa 109:13-15), hence children may glory in virtuous ancestry.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 7. Excellent speech — (Compare Margin). Such language as ill suits a fool, as lying (ought to suit) a prince (Pr 16:12, 13).

entries.title: Proverbs 17:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. One so corrupt as to take a bribe evinces his high estimate of it by subjection to its influence (Pr 18:16; 19:6).

entries.title: Proverbs 17:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. seeketh love — (Compare Margin). The contrast is between the peace-maker and tale-bearer.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. Reproof more affects the wise than severe scourging, fools.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. Such meet just retribution (1Ki 2:25). a cruel messenger — one to inflict it.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. They are less rational in anger than wild beasts.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. (Compare Psa 7:4; 35:12). evil — injury to another (Pr 13:21).

entries.title: Proverbs 17:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. letteth... water — as a breach in a dam. before... meddled with — before strife has become sharp, or, by an explanation better suiting the figure, before it rolls on, or increases.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. abomination... Lord — as reversing His method of acting (Pr 3:32; 12:2).

entries.title: Proverbs 17:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16. Though wealth cannot buy wisdom for those who do not love it, yet wisdom procures wealth (Pr 3:16; 14:24).

entries.title: Proverbs 17:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. To the second of these parallel clauses, there is an accession of meaning, that is, that a brother's love is specially seen in adversity.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18. (Compare Pr 6:1-5; 11:15). in the presence, &c. — that is, he either fails to consult his friend, or to follow his advice.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19. strife — contention is, and leads to, sin. he that exalteth his gate — gratifies a vain love of costly building. seeketh — or, "findeth," as if he sought (compare "loveth death," Pr 8:36).

entries.title: Proverbs 17:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. The second clause advances on the first. The ill-natured fail of good, and the cavilling and fault-finding incur evil.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21. (Compare Pr 23:24). Different words are rendered by "fool," both denoting stupidity and impiety.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22. (Compare Pr 14:30; 15:13). The effect of the mind on the body is well known. medicine — or, "body," which better corresponds with "bone." drieth — as if the marrow were exhausted.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23. a gift... bosom — Money and other valuables were borne in a fold of the garment, called the bosom. to pervert — that is, by bribery.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 24. Wisdom... him — ever an object of regard, while a fool's affections are unsettled.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 25. a grief — or cross, vexation (compare Pr 17:21; 10:1).

entries.title: Proverbs 17:26
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26. Also — that is, Equally to be avoided are other sins: punishing good subjects, or resisting good rulers.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:27–28
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 27-28. Prudence of speech is commended as is an excellent or calm spirit, not excited to vain conversation.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 18 Pr 18:1-24. 1. Through desire... seeketh — that is, seeks selfish gratification. intermeddleth... wisdom — or, "rushes on" (Pr 17:14) against all wisdom, or what is valuable (Pr 2:7).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. that his heart... itself — that is, takes pleasure in revealing his folly (Pr 12:23; 15:2).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. So surely are sin and punishment connected (Pr 16:4). wicked, for "wickedness," answers to ignominy, or the state of such; and contempt, the feeling of others to them; and to reproach, a manifestation of contempt.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4. Wise speech is like an exhaustless stream of benefit.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5. accept the person — (Compare Psa 82:2). "It is not good" is to be supplied before "to overthrow."

entries.title: Proverbs 18:6–7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6-7. The quarrelsome bring trouble on themselves. Their rash language ensnares them (Pr 6:2).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. (Compare Pr 16:28). as wounds — not sustained by the Hebrew; better, as "sweet morsels," which men gladly swallow. innermost... belly — the mind, or heart (compare Pr 20:27-30; Psa 22:14).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. One by failing to get, the other by wasting wealth, grows poor. waster — literally, "master of washing," a prodigal.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. name of the Lord — manifested perfections (Psa 8:1; 20:2), as faithfulness, power, mercy, &c., on which men rely. is safe — literally, "set on high, out of danger" (Psa 18:2; 91:4).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. contrasts with Pr 18:10 (compare Pr 10:15). Such is a vain trust (compare Psa 73:6).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 18:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. Hasty speech evinces self-conceit, and ensures shame (Pr 26:12).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. infirmity — bodily sickness, or outward evil. The spirit, which sustains, being wounded, no support is left, except, as implied, in God.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 18:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16. (Compare Pr 17:8, 23). Disapproval of the fact stated is implied.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. One-sided statements are not reliable. searcheth — thoroughly (Pr 17:9, 19).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18. The lot — whose disposal is of God (Pr 16:13), may, properly used, be a right mode of settling disputes.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19. No feuds so difficult of adjustment as those of relatives; hence great care should be used to avoid them.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. (Compare Pr 12:14; 13:2). Men's words are the fruit, or, increase of his lips, and when good, benefit them. satisfied with — (Compare Pr 1:31; 14:14).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21. Death and life — or, the greatest evil and good. that love it — that is, the tongue, or its use for good or evil. eat... fruit — (Compare Pr 18:19; Jas 1:19).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22. The old versions supply "good" before the "wife," as the last clause and Pr 19:14 imply (compare Pr 31:10).

entries.title: Proverbs 18:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23. the rich... roughly — He is tolerated because rich, implying that the estimate of men by wealth is wrong.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 24. A man... friendly — better, "A man... (is) to, or, may triumph (Psa 108:9), or, shout for joy (Psa 5:11), that is, may congratulate himself." Indeed, there is a Friend who is better than a brother; such is the "Friend of sinners" [Mt 11:19; Lu 7:34], who may have been before the writer's mind.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 19 Pr 19:1-29. 1. (Compare Pr 28:6). "Rich" for fool here. Integrity is better than riches (Pr 15:16, 17; 16:8).

entries.title: Proverbs 19:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. The last illustrates the first clause. Rashness, the result of ignorance, brings trouble.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. perverteth... way — turns him back from right (Pr 13:6; Jas 1:13); and he blames God for his failures.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4. (Compare Pr 14:20). Such facts are often adduced with implied disapprobation.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5. Compare Pr 19:9, where perish explains not escape here (compare Psa 88:9, 10).

entries.title: Proverbs 19:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. (Compare Margin; Pr 15:32). loveth... soul — or, "himself," which he evinces by regarding his best interests. keepeth — or, "regards."

entries.title: Proverbs 19:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. (Compare Pr 17:7). The fool is incapable of properly using pleasure as knowledge, yet for him to have it is less incongruous than the undue elevation of servants. Let each abide in his calling (1Co 7:20).

entries.title: Proverbs 19:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. (Compare Pr 14:29; 16:32). This inculcation of a forgiving spirit shows that true religion is always the same (Mt 5:22-24).

entries.title: Proverbs 19:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. (Compare Pr 16:14, 15; 20:2). A motive to submission to lawful authority.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. calamity — literally, "calamities," varied and many. continual dropping — a perpetual annoyance, wearing out patience.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. A contrast of men's gifts and God's, who, though author of both blessings, confers the latter by His more special providence. and — or, "but," implying that the evils of Pr 19:13 are only avoided by His care.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. a deep sleep — a state of utter indifference. idle soul — or, "person" (compare Pr 10:4; 12:24).

entries.title: Proverbs 19:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16. (Compare Pr 10:17; 13:13). despiseth... ways — opposed to keeping or observing, neglects (Pr 16:17) (as unworthy of regard) his moral conduct.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. (Compare Pr 14:21; Psa 37:26). hath pity — shown by acts (compare Margin).

entries.title: Proverbs 19:18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18. (Compare Pr 13:24; 23:13). let not... spare — literally, "do not lift up thy soul" (Psa 24:4; 25:1), that is, do not desire to his death; a caution to passionate parents against angry chastisement.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19. Repeated efforts of kindness are lost on ill-natured persons.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. (Compare Pr 13:18-20). latter end — (Pr 5:11). In youth prepare for age.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21. (Compare Pr 16:1, 9; Psa 33:10, 11). The failure of man's devices is implied.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22. desire — that is, to do good, indicates a kind disposition (Pr 11:23); and the poor thus affected are better than liars, who say and do not.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23. The fear... life — (Compare Pr 3:2). abide — or, "remain contented" (1Ti 4:8). not visited with evil — (Pr 10:3; Psa 37:25), as a judgment, in which sense visit is often used (Psa 89:32; Jr 6:15).

entries.title: Proverbs 19:24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 24. bosom — literally, a wide dish in which the hand was plunged in eating (Mt 26:23). Compare Pr 26:15, the sentiment expressed with equal irony and less exaggeration.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 25. Such is the benefit of reproof; even the simple profit, much more the wise.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:26
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26. Unfilial conduct often condemned (Pr 17:21-25; 20:20; De 21:18, 21).

entries.title: Proverbs 19:27
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 27. Avoid whatever leads from truth.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:28
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 28. ungodly witness — (Compare Margin), one false by bad principles (compare Pr 6:12). scorneth judgment — sets at naught the dictates of justice. devoureth — literally, "swalloweth," as something delightful.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:29
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 29. Their punishment is sure, fixed, and ready (compare Pr 3:34; 10:13).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 20 Pr 20:1-30. 1. mocker — scorner. Such men are made by wine. strong drink — made by spicing wine (compare Is 5:11, 22); and it may include wine. raging — or boisterous as a drunkard. deceived — literally, "erring," or reeling.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. (Compare Pr 19:12). Men who resist authority injure themselves (Ro 13:2).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. to cease from strife — or, better, "to dwell from or without strife," denoting the habit of life. fool... meddling — (Pr 17:14).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4. shall... beg — literally, "ask" (in this sense, Psa 109:10).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5. Counsel... water — that is, deeply hidden (Pr 18:4; Psa 13:2). The wise can discern well.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:6
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6. Boasters are unreliable. goodness — or, "kind disposition."

entries.title: Proverbs 20:7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 7. The conduct of good men proclaims their sound principles. God's covenant and their good example secure blessing to their children (Pr 4:26; Psa 112:1, 2).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. As in Pr 14:35; 16:10, 15, this is the character of a good king, not of all kings.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. The interrogation in the affirmative strengthens the implied negation (compare Job 15:14; Ec 7:20).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. Various measures, implying that some are wrong (compare Pr 11:1; 16:11).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. The conduct of children even is the best test of principle (compare Mt 7:16).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. Hence, of course, God will know all you do (Psa 94:9).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. Activity and diligence contrasted with sloth (Pr 6:9; 10:11). lest... poverty — literally, "be deprived of inheritance."

entries.title: Proverbs 20:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. when... his way — implying that he goes about boasting of his bargains.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. The contrast denotes the greater value of knowledge (compare Pr 3:14-16).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16. Take his garment — implies severe exaction, justified by the surety's rashness. a strange woman — by some readings "strangers," but the former here, and in Pr 27:13, is allowable, and strengthens the sense. The debauchee is less reliable than the merely careless.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. Bread... sweet — either as unlawfully (Pr 9:17) or easily obtained. mouth... gravel — well expresses the pain and grief given at last.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18. (Compare Pr 15:22). Be careful and considerate in important plans.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19. Those who love to tell news will hardly keep secrets. flattereth... lips — (compare Margin; Pr 1:10). meddle... him — literally, "join," or "associate with."

entries.title: Proverbs 20:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. his lamp — (Compare Pr 13:9; 24:20).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21. gotten hastily — contrary to God's providence (Pr 28:20), implying its unjust or easy attainment; hence the man is punished, or spends freely what he got easily (compare Pr 20:17).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 20:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 20:24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 24. Man's goings — literally, "Stately steppings of a strong man." a man — any common man. understand — or, "perceive."

entries.title: Proverbs 20:25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 25. devoureth... holy — or, better, "who rashly speaks promises," or "devotes what is holy," consecrating any thing. This suits better the last clause, which expresses a similar view of the results of rashly vowing.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:26
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26. (Compare Pr 20:8). bringeth... over them — The wheel was used for threshing grain. The figure denotes severity (compare Am 1:3).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:27
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 27. The spirit... Lord — Men's minds are God's gifts, and thus able to search one another (compare Pr 20:5; Pr 18:8, 17; 1Co 2:11).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:28
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 20:29
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 29. The glory of young men... the beauty of old men — Each age has its peculiar excellence (Pr 16:31).

entries.title: Proverbs 20:30
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 30. blueness — literally, "joining," the process of uniting the edges of a wound throws off purulent matter. stripes... belly — So punishment provides healing of soul (Pr 18:8), by deterring from evil courses.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 21 Pr 21:1-31. 1. rivers — irrigating channels (Psa 1:3), whose course was easily turned (compare De 11:10). God disposes even kings as He pleases (Pr 16:9; Psa 33:15).

entries.title: Proverbs 21:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 21:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 21:4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4. high look — (Compare Margin; Psa 131:1). proud heart — or, "heart of breadth," one that is swollen (compare Psa 101:5). ploughing — better "lamp," a frequent figure for prosperity (Pr 20:20); hence joy or delight.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5. The contrast is between steady industry and rashness (compare Pr 19:2).

entries.title: Proverbs 21:6
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6. The getting — or, "what is obtained" (compare Job 7:2; Jr 22:13, Hebrew). vanity... to and fro — as fleeting as chaff or stubble in the wind (compare Pr 20:17-21; Psa 62:10). Such gettings are unsatisfactory. them... death — act as if they did (Pr 8:36; 17:19).

entries.title: Proverbs 21:7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 7. robbery — or, "destruction," especially oppression, of which they are authors. shall destroy — literally, "cut with a saw" (1Ki 7:9), that is, utterly ruin them. Their sins shall be visited on them in kind. to do judgment — what is just and right.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. of man — any one; his way is opposed to truth, and also estranged from it. The pure proves himself such by his right conduct.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. corner — a turret or arbor on the roof. brawling — or contentious. wide house — literally, "house of fellowship," large enough for several families.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. So strongly does he desire to do evil (Psa 10:3; Ec 8:11), that he will not even spare his friend if in his way.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. (Compare Pr 19:25). That which the simple learn by the terrors of punishment, the wise learn by teaching.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. (Compare Psa 37:35-38; 73:17, 20). house — family or interests. overthroweth — either supply "God" (compare Pr 10:24), or the word is used impersonally.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. The principles of retribution, often taught (compare Psa 18:26; Mt 7:1-12).

entries.title: Proverbs 21:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. The effect of bribery (Pr 17:23) is enhanced by secrecy, as the bribed person does not wish his motives made known.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. But the just love right and need no bribes. The wicked at last meet destruction, though for a time happy in concealing corruption.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16. the way of understanding — (Compare Pr 12:26; 14:22). remain — that is, rest as at a journey's end; death will be his unchanging home.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. Costly luxuries impoverish.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18. (Compare Pr 11:8). By suffering what they had devised for the righteous, or brought on them, the wicked became their ransom, in the usual sense of substitutes (compare Jos 7:26; Es 7:9).

entries.title: Proverbs 21:19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19. (Compare Pr 21:9). wilderness — pasture, though uninhabitable ground (Psa 65:12).

entries.title: Proverbs 21:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. The wise, by diligence and care, lay up and increase wealth, while fools spend — literally, "swallow it up," greedily.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21. He who tries to act justly and kindly (Psa 34:14) will prosper and obtain justice and honor.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22. "Wisdom is better than strength" (Ec 7:19; 9:15). strength... thereof — that in which they confide.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 21:24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 24. The reproachful name is deserved by those who treat others with anger and contempt.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 25. desire — that is, of ease and idleness brings him to starvation.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:26
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26. The sin of covetousness marks the sluggard, as the virtue of benevolence the righteous.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:27
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 27. God regards the heart, and hypocrisy is more odious than open inconsistency. wicked mind — or, "design" (Pr 1:4).

entries.title: Proverbs 21:28
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 28. (Compare Pr 19:5). that heareth — or heeds instruction, and so grows wise. speaketh constantly — or sincerely (compare Ha 1:5), and hence is believed (Pr 12:19; Jas 1:19).

entries.title: Proverbs 21:29
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 29. hardeneth his face — is obstinate. directeth... way — considers it, and acts advisedly.

entries.title: Proverbs 21:30–31
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 30-31. Men's best devices and reliances are vain compared with God's, or without His aid (Pr 19:21; Psa 20:7; 33:17).

entries.title: Proverbs 22:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 22 Pr 22:1-29. 1. A good name — (Job 30:8, Hebrew); "good" is supplied here from Ec 7:1. loving favour — kind regard, that is, of the wise and good.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. Before God all are on the same footing (Pr 14:31; 17:5).

entries.title: Proverbs 22:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. are punished — that is, for their temerity; for the evil is not necessarily punitive, as the prudent might otherwise be its objects.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4. humility and the fear of the Lord — are in apposition; one produces the other. On the results, compare Pr 3:16; 8:18.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5. he that... them — Those who properly watch over their own souls are thus preserved from the dangers which attend the way of perverse men (Pr 16:17).

entries.title: Proverbs 22:6
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6. Train — initiate, or early instruct. the way — literally, "his way," that selected for him in which he should go; for early training secures habitual walking in it.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 7. The influence of wealth sets aside moral distinctions is implied, and, of course, disapproved (compare Pr 19:6; 21:14, &c.).

entries.title: Proverbs 22:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. (Compare Pr 11:18; Psa 109:16-20; Ga 6:7, 8). the rod... fail — His power to do evil will be destroyed.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. a bountiful eye — that is, a beneficent disposition. for he giveth... poor — His acts prove it.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. Cast out — or drive away. Scorners foster strife by taunts and revilings.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. (Compare Margin). pureness of heart — and gentle, kind words win favor, even from kings.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. preserve — or guard. knowledge — its principles and possessors. overthroweth — utterly confounds and destroys the wicked.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. Frivolous excuses satisfy the indolent man's conscience.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. The mouth — or flattering speeches (Pr 5:3; 7:5) ensnare man, as pits, beasts. God makes their own sin their punishment.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. is bound — or firmly fixed. Chastisement deters from crime and so leads to reformation of principle.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16. These two vices pertain to the same selfish feeling. Both are deservedly odious to God and incur punishment.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. Here begins another division of the book, marked by those encouragements to the pursuit of wisdom, which are found in the earlier chapters. It will be observed that at Pr 22:22-24:12, the proverbs are generally expressed in two verses instead of one (see Introduction).

entries.title: Proverbs 22:18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18. These lessons must be laid up in the mind, and fitted — or better, "fixed" in the lips so as to be ever ready.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19. That... Lord — This is the design of the instruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. excellent things — or probably of former times. counsels and knowledge — both advice and instruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21. Specially he desires to secure accuracy, so that his pupil may teach others.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:22–23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22-23. Here follow ten precepts of two verses each. Though men fail to defend the poor, God will (Pr 17:5; Psa 12:5). in the gate — place of public gathering (Job 5:4; Psa 69:12).

entries.title: Proverbs 22:24–25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 22:26–27
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 22:28
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 28. (Compare Pr 23:10). Do not entrench on others (De 19:14; 27:17).

entries.title: Proverbs 22:29
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 29. Success rewards diligence (Pr 10:4; 21:5).

entries.title: Proverbs 23:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 23 Pr 23:1-35. 1. Avoid the dangers of gluttony.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. put a knife — an Eastern figure for putting restraint on the appetite.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. are deceitful meat — though well tasted, injurious.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:4–5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4-5. (Compare 1Ti 6:9, 10). thine own wisdom — which regards riches intrinsically as a blessing.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:6–8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6-8. Beware of deceitful men, whose courtesies even you will repent of having accepted. evil eye — or purpose (Pr 22:9; De 15:9; Mt 6:23).

entries.title: Proverbs 23:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. (Compare Pr 9:8). "Cast not your pearls before swine" (Mt 7:6).

entries.title: Proverbs 23:10–11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 23:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. Here begins another series of precepts.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:13–14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13-14. While there is little danger that the use of the "divine ordinance of the rod" will produce bodily harm, there is great hope of spiritual good.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:15–16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15-16. The pleasure afforded the teacher by the pupil's progress is a motive to diligence.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:17–18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17-18. (Compare Margin). The prosperity of the wicked is short.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:19–21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19-21. guide... way — or direct thy thoughts to a right course of conduct (compare Pr 4:4; 9:6).

entries.title: Proverbs 23:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22. Hearken — that is, obey (Pr 1:8; Ep 6:1). despise... old — Adults revere the parents whom, as children, they once obeyed.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23. Buy — literally, "get" (Pr 4:5). truth — generally and specially as opposed to errors of all kinds.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:24–25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 23:26–35
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26-35. A solemn warning against whoredom and drunkenness (Ho 4:11). give me — This is the address of that divine wisdom so often presented (Pr 8:1; 9:3, &c.). heart — confidence. observe — keep. my ways — such as I teach you (Pr 3:17; 9:6).

entries.title: Proverbs 24:1–2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 24 Pr 24:1-34. 1-2. (Compare Pr 23:3, 17; Psa 37:1).

entries.title: Proverbs 24:3–4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3-4. (Compare Pr 14:1; Is 54:14). house — including the family.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:5–6
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5-6. The general statement (Ec 9:16, 18) is specially illustrated (compare Pr 21:22; Psa 144:1).

entries.title: Proverbs 24:7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 7. (Compare Pr 14:16). in the gate — (Compare Pr 22:22).

entries.title: Proverbs 24:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. So called even if he fails to do evil.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. Same thought varied.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. Literally, "If thou fail in the day of straits (adversity), strait (or, small) is thy strength," which is then truly tested.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:11–12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11-12. Neglect of known duty is sin (Jas 4:17). ready — literally, "bowing down" to be slain — that is, unjustly. God's retributive justice cannot be avoided by professed ignorance.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:13–14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13-14. As delicious food whets the appetite, so should the rewards of wisdom excite us to seek it.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:15–16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15-16. The plots of the wicked against the good, though partially, shall not be fully successful (Psa 37:24); while the wicked, falling under penal evil, find no help.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:17–18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17-18. Yet let none rejoice over the fate of evildoers, lest God punish their wrong spirit by relieving the sufferer (compare Pr 17:5; Job 31:29).

entries.title: Proverbs 24:19–20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 24:21–22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21-22. A warning against impiety and resistance to lawful rule (Ro 13:1-7; 1Pe 2:17). meddle... change — (Compare Margin), literally, "mingle not yourself," avoid the society of restless persons.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23. These... wise — literally, "are of the wise," as authors (compare "Psalms of David," Hebrew). "These" refers to the verses following, Pr 24:24-34. to have respect — literally, "to discern faces," show partiality,

entries.title: Proverbs 24:24–25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 24-25. of which an example is justifying the wicked, to which is opposed, rebuking him, which has a blessing.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:26
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26. kiss his lips — love and obey, do homage (Psa 2:12; So 8:1). right answer — literally, "plain words" (compare Pr 8:9), opposed to deceptive, or obscure.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:27
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 27. Prepare... in the field — Secure, by diligence, a proper support, and then build; provide necessaries, then comforts, to which a house rather pertained, in a mild climate, permitting the use of tents.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:28
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 28. Do not speak even truth needlessly against any, and never falsehood.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:29
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 29. Especially avoid retaliation (Mt 5:43-45; Ro 12:17).

entries.title: Proverbs 24:30–31
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 30-31. A striking picture of the effects of sloth.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:32–34
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 32-34. From the folly of the sluggard learn wisdom (Pr 6:10, 11).

entries.title: Proverbs 25:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 25 Pr 25:1-28. 1. The character of these proverbs sustains the title (see Introduction). also — refers to the former part of the book. copied out — literally, "transferred," that is, from some other book to this; not given from memory.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. God's unsearchableness impresses us with awe (compare Is 45:15; Ro 11:33). But kings, being finite, should confer with wise counsellors;

entries.title: Proverbs 25:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. Ye wisely keeping state secrets, which to common men are as inaccessible heights and depths.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:4–5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4-5. As separating impurities from ore leaves pure silver, so taking from a king wicked counsellors leaves a wise and beneficent government.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:6–7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6-7. Do not intrude into the presence of the king, for the elevation of the humble is honorable, but the humbling of the proud disgraceful (Lu 14:8-10).

entries.title: Proverbs 25:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. (Compare Pr 3:30). lest... shame — lest you do what you ought not, when shamed by defeat, or "lest thou art shut out from doing any thing."

entries.title: Proverbs 25:9–10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9-10. (Compare Mt 5:25, Margin). secret — that is, of your opponent, for his disadvantage, and so you be disgraced, not having discussed your difficulties with him.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. a word fitly — literally, "quickly," as wheels roll, just in time. The comparison as apples... silver gives a like sense. apples, &c. — either real apples of golden color, in a silver network basket, or imitations on silver embroidery.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. Those who desire to know and do rightly, most highly esteem good counsel (Pr 9:9; 15:31). The listening ear is better than one hung with gold.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. Snow from mountains was used to cool drinks; so refreshing is a faithful messenger (Pr 13:17).

entries.title: Proverbs 25:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. clouds — literally, "vapors" (Jr 10:13), clouds only in appearance. a false gift — promised, but not given.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. Gentleness and kindness overcome the most powerful and obstinate. long forbearing — or, "slowness to anger" (Pr 14:29; 15:18).

entries.title: Proverbs 25:16–17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16-17. A comparison, as a surfeit of honey produces physical disgust, so your company, however agreeable in moderation, may, if excessive, lead your friend to hate you.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18. A false witness is as destructive to reputation, as such weapons to the body (Pr 24:28). beareth... witness — literally, "answereth questions," as before a judge, against his neighbor.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19. Treachery annoys as well as deceives.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. Not only is the incongruity of songs (that is, joyful) and sadness meant, but an accession of sadness, by want of sympathy, is implied.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:21–22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21-22. (Compare Mt 5:44; Ro 12:20). As metals are melted by heaping coals upon them, so is the heart softened by kindness.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23. Better, "As the north wind bringeth forth (Psa 90:2) or produces rain, so does a concealed or slandering tongue produce anger."

entries.title: Proverbs 25:24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 25:25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 25. (Compare Pr 25:13). good news — that is, of some loved interest or absent friend, the more grateful as coming from afar.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:26
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26. From troubled fountains and corrupt springs no healthy water is to be had, so when the righteous are oppressed by the wicked, their power for good is lessened or destroyed.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:27
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 27. Satiety surfeits (Pr 25:16); so men who are self-glorious find shame. is not glory — "not" is supplied from the first clause, or "is grievous," in which sense a similar word is used (Pr 27:2).

entries.title: Proverbs 25:28
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 28. Such are exposed to the incursions of evil thoughts and successful temptations.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 26 Pr 26:1-28. 1. The incongruities of nature illustrate also those of the moral world. The fool's unworthiness is also implied (Pr 17:7; 19:10).

entries.title: Proverbs 26:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. Though not obvious to us, the bird — literally, "sparrow" — and swallow — have an object in their motions, so penal evil falls on none without a reason.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. The rod is as much needed by fools and as well suited to them, as whips and bridles are for beasts.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:4–5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4-5. Answer not — that is, approvingly by like folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:6
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6. A fool fails by folly as surely as if he were maimed. drinketh damage — that is, gets it abundantly (Job 15:16; 34:7).

entries.title: Proverbs 26:7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 7. legs... equal — or, "take away the legs," or "the legs... are weak." In any case the idea is that they are the occasion of an awkwardness, such as the fool shows in using a parable or proverb (see Introduction; Pr 17:7).

entries.title: Proverbs 26:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. A stone, bound in a sling, is useless; so honor, conferred on a fool, is thrown away.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. As vexatious and unmanageable as a thorn in a drunkard's hand is a parable to a fool. He will be as apt to misuse is as to use it rightly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. Various versions of this are proposed (compare Margin). Better perhaps — "Much He injures (or literally, "wounds") all who reward," &c., that is, society is injured by encouraging evil men. transgressors — may be rendered "vagrants." The word "God" is improperly supplied.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. returneth... folly — Though disgusting to others, the fool delights in his folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. The self-conceited are taught with more difficulty than the stupid.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. (Compare Pr 22:13).

entries.title: Proverbs 26:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 26:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. (Compare Pr 19:24).

entries.title: Proverbs 26:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16. The thoughtless being ignorant of their ignorance are conceited.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. meddleth — as in Pr 20:19; 24:21; as either holding a dog by the ears or letting him go involves danger, so success in another man's strife or failure involves a useless risk of reputation, does no good, and may do us harm.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:18–19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18-19. Such are reckless of results.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:20–21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20-21. The talebearers foster (Pr 16:28), and the contentious excite, strife.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22. (Compare Pr 18:8).

entries.title: Proverbs 26:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23. Warm professions can no more give value to insincerity than silver coating to rude earthenware.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 24. dissembleth — though an unusual sense of the word (compare Margin), is allowable, and better suits the context, which sets forth hypocrisy.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 25. Sentiment of Pr 26:24 carried out. seven abominations in his heart — that is, very many (compare Pr 24:16).

entries.title: Proverbs 26:26–27
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26-27. Deceit will at last be exposed, and the wicked by their own arts often bring on retribution (compare Pr 12:13; Psa 7:16; 9:17, &c.).

entries.title: Proverbs 26:28
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 28. Men hate those they injure. A lying tongue — "lips" for the persons (compare Pr 4:24; Psa 12:3).

entries.title: Proverbs 27:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 27 Pr 27:1-27. 1. Do not confide implicitly in your plans (Pr 16:9; 19:21; Jas 4:13-15).

entries.title: Proverbs 27:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. Avoid self-praise.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. heavy — The literal sense of "heavy," applied to material subjects, illustrates its figurative, "grievous," applied to moral. a fool's wrath — is unreasonable and excessive.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4. envy — or, "jealousy" (compare Margin; Pr 6:34), is more unappeasable than the simpler bad passions.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:5–6
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5-6. secret love — not manifested in acts is useless; and even, if its exhibition by rebukes wounds us, such love is preferable to the frequent (compare Margin), and hence deceitful, kisses of an enemy.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 7. The luxury of wealth confers less happiness than the healthy appetite of labor.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. Such are not only out of place, but out of duty and in danger.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. rejoice the heart — the organ of perceiving what pleases the senses. sweetness... counsel — or, "wise counsel is also pleasing."

entries.title: Proverbs 27:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. Adhere to tried friends. The ties of blood may be less reliable than those of genuine friendship.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. The wisdom of children both reflects credit on parents and contributes to their aid in difficulties.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:12–13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown

entries.title: Proverbs 27:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. Excessive zeal in praising raises suspicions of selfishness.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. (Compare Pr 19:13). very... day — literally, "a day of showers."

entries.title: Proverbs 27:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16. hideth — or, "restrains" (that is, tries to do it); is as fruitless an effort, as that of holding the wind. the ointment of his right hand — the organ of power (Psa 17:7; 18:35). His right hand endeavors to repress perfume, but vainly. Some prefer: "His right hand comes on oil," that is, "cannot take hold." Such a woman cannot be tamed.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. a man sharpeneth... friend — that is, conversation promotes intelligence, which the face exhibits.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18. Diligence secures a reward, even for the humble servant.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19. We may see our characters in the developed tempers of others.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. Men's cupidity is as insatiable as the grave.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21. Praise tests character. a man to his praise — according to his praise, as he bears it. Thus vain men seek it, weak men are inflated by it, wise men disregard it, &c.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22. The obstinate wickedness of such is incurable by the heaviest inflictions.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:23–24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23-24. flocks — constituted the staple of wealth. It is only by care and diligence that the most solid possessions can be perpetuated (Pr 23:5).

entries.title: Proverbs 27:25–27
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 25-27. The fact that providential arrangements furnish the means of competence to those who properly use them is another motive to diligence (compare Psa 65:9-13). The hay appeareth — literally, "Grass appeareth" (Job 40:15; Psa 104:14).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:1
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: CHAPTER 28 Pr 28:1-28. 1. A bad conscience makes men timid; the righteous are alone truly bold (Pr 14:26; Psa 27:1).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:2
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 2. Anarchy producing contending rulers shortens the reign of each. but by a man... prolonged — or, "by a man of understanding — that is, a good ruler — he who knows or regards the right, that is, a good citizen, shall prolong (his days)." Good rulers are a blessing to the people. Bad government as a punishment for evil is contrasted with good as blessing to the good.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:3
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 3. A poor man, &c. — Such, in power, exact more severely, and so leave subjects bare.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:4
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 4. They that forsake... wicked — Wrongdoers encourage one another.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:5
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 5. (Compare Joh 7:17). Ignorance of moral truth is due to unwillingness to know it.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:6
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 6. (Compare Pr 10:6). Riches cannot compensate for sin, nor the want of them affect integrity.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:7
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 7. (Compare Pr 17:25). riotous men — or, "gluttons" (Pr 23:20, 21).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:8
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 8. usury... unjust gain — (Compare Margin). The two terms, meaning nearly the same, may denote excessive interest. God's providence directs the proper use of wealth.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:9
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 9. (Compare Pr 15:8; 21:27). hearing — that is, obeying. God requires sincere worshippers (Psa 66:18; Joh 4:24).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:10
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 10. (Compare Pr 26:27).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:11
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 11. A poor but wise man can discover (and expose) the rich and self-conceited.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:12
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 12. great glory — or, cause for it to a people, for the righteous rejoice in good, and righteousness exalts a nation (Pr 14:34). a man... hidden — that is, the good retire, or all kinds try to escape a wicked rule.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:13
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 13. (Compare Psa 32:3-5). Concealment of sin delivers none from God's wrath, but He shows mercy to the humble penitent (Psa 51:4).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:14
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 14. feareth — that is, God, and so repents. hardeneth his heart — makes himself insensible to sin, and so will not repent (Pr 14:16; 29:1).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:15
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 15. The rapacity and cruelty of such beasts well represent some wicked men (compare Psa 7:2; 17:12).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:16
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 16. The prince... understanding — that is, He does not perceive that oppression jeopards his success. Covetousness often produces oppression, hence the contrast.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:17
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 17. doeth violence... blood, &c. — or, that is oppressed by the blood of life (Ge 9:6), which he has taken. to the pit — the grave or destruction (Pr 1:12; Job 33:18-24; Psa 143:7). stay him — sustain or deliver him.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:18
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 18. (Compare Pr 10:9; 17:20). Double dealing is eventually fatal.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:19
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 19. (Compare Pr 10:4; 20:4). vain persons — idle, useless drones, implying that they are also wicked (Pr 12:11; Psa 26:4).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:20
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 20. maketh haste... rich — implying deceit or fraud (Pr 20:21), and so opposed to "faithful" or reliable.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:21
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 21. respect of persons — (Pr 24:23). Such are led to evil by the slightest motive.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:22
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 22. (Compare Pr 28:20). evil eye — in the general sense of Pr 23:6, here more specific for covetousness (compare Pr 22:9; Mt 20:15). poverty... him — by God's providence.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:23
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 23. (Compare Pr 9:8, 9; 27:5). Those benefited by reproof will love their monitors.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:24
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 24. (Compare Mt 15:4-6). Such, though heirs, are virtually thieves, to be ranked with highwaymen.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:25
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 25. of a proud heart — literally, "puffed up of soul" — that is, self-confident, and hence overbearing and litigious. made fat — or, "prosperous" (Pr 11:25; 16:20).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:26
entries.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset, and David Brown
entries.content: 26. (Compare Pr 3:6-8). walketh wisely — that is, trusting in God (Pr 22:17-19).

entries.title: Proverbs 28:27
